newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rate steady on lack of factors.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rate steady on lack of factors.

text.p: Philippine interbank call loan rates were locked in the same range of 10.75 to 10.53125 percent on a dearth of market-moving developments, traders said on Thursday.
The average rate was unchanged at 10.53125 percent. There were 22 lenders and 15 borrowers.
"The borrowers were usually the smaller banks. There were a couple of big banks borrowing in small volumes," a trader said.
Banks had been awash with liquidity because of a new 20 percent tax imposed on term reverse repos which had discouraged them from reinvesting their money.
And the Central Bank had maintained its overnight borrowing rate at 10.5 percent, traders said.
In the secondary market, banks were buying 91-day T-bills to service their clients' requirements.
Moreover, they have opted to buy more of the six-month rather than the one-year bills since rates on the one year are now "too low," a dealer said.
A Reuter poll of eight financial institutions showed bid rates ranging from 10.665 to 10.725 on the three-month bills; 11.05 to 11.20 on the six months; and 11.50 to 11.65 on the one-year bills.
